LESSON: TYPES OF BUSINESS OWNERSHIP

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Business and its Environment
Topic 2.2: Types of Business Ownership
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Types of Business Ownership, part of Business and its Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are sole proprietorship, partnerships and cooperative societies formed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore the formation, management, sources of finance, advantages, and disadvantages of a sole proprietorship business enterprise in Kenya,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Types of Business Ownership together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner enhances reading, writing, listening, speaking and teamwork skills

when discussing, brainstorming and presenting on the meaning, formation and management of sole proprietorship,

partnerships and cooperative societies.

● Learning to learn: learner organises own learning when using digital devices with assistive technology or print or

braille media to search for sources of finance for sole proprietorship, partnerships and cooperative societies in

Kenya.

● Self-efficacy: learner develops the skill of effective communication when debating on the advantages and

disadvantages of a sole proprietorship, partnerships and cooperative societies in Kenya.

Values:
● Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when discussing and presenting on the meaning of sole

proprietorship, partnership and cooperative society.

● Love: learner respects others when sharing digital devices with assistive technology or printer or braille media to

search for information.

● Responsibility: learner shows accountability when using digital devices with assistive technology or print or braille

media to search for information on sources of finance for sole proprietorship, partnerships and cooperative

societies.

present case studies on the sole proprietorship, partnerships and cooperative societies.
